batch_node.name: AWS dimensions v0.2.0
batch_node.description: Declares every dimension aws_core writes: tap.cloud (the model and edge default) and cloud, aws_account and aws_region (stamped by the collector on every node it writes). v0.2.0 renames the v0.1.0 node from 'tap.cloud: aws' to its key 'tap.cloud' (same entity id) and adds the three collector keys, so each key in use has a declared Dimension node before core's dimension-map reshape (tap#708, #711). A new batch id, because an already-imported batch is skipped on re-seed.

node.name: tap.cloud
node.description: Which cloud provider an entity belongs to. Every aws_core model and edge type declares it as a default dimension with the value "aws", so every AWS node and edge carries {"tap.cloud": "aws"} from the moment it is created.

node.name: cloud
node.description: The cloud provider, as the aws_core collector stamps it on every node it writes in a run (value "aws"), alongside aws_account and aws_region. It carries the same fact as tap.cloud, which comes from the model defaults rather than the collector. Declared under its current name; whether to keep both is an open question.

node.name: aws_account
node.description: The AWS account a resource is in: the twelve-digit account id of the collector's credential (STS GetCallerIdentity), stamped on every node and edge the collector writes. It replaces a BELONGS_TO_ACCOUNT edge from every resource, which would make the account node a hub (req-aws-core-account-dimension). For a resource shared in from another account through AWS RAM it records the observing account, and the BELONGS_TO_ACCOUNT edge names the owner. The falsifiers compare it with their own credential's account to decide whether they can speak to a resource's absence.

node.name: aws_region
node.description: The AWS region a resource was read in (for example us-east-1 or us-gov-west-1), stamped by the collector on every node it writes. A global-scope resource, and the Organizations tree, carry the value "global". The falsifiers read it as the region to probe.
